mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.7% (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.7%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing equity discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through lower cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.7% occurs in 70% of cases but 20-day forward returns are negative in > 55% of those instances (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 4.5% (UNRATE < 4.5%) signals robust labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending power and driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns via elevated corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.5% occurs in 65% of cases but 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS (≤ 0.7%) and CPIAUCSL (≤ 2.5% YoY) indicates monetary easing with stable inflation, compressing equity risk premia and producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.7% AND CPIAUCSL ≤ 2.5% occurs but 20-day returns are negative in > 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes with strong GDP growth (GDPC1 growth > 3% YoY), rising housing starts (HOUST > 1250) signal sustained consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Late-cycle expansion with GDPC1 growth > 3% YoY and HOUST > 1250 occurs but 60-day returns are negative in > 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline below 100 (INDPRO < 100) indicates weakening manufacturing output, triggering negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to reduced corporate earnings forecasts.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 occurs in 60% of cases but 5-day returns are positive in > 55% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1250 thousand units (HOUST > 1250) reflect strong residential construction activity, boosting consumer confidence and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1250 occurs but 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment growth exceeding 0.5% monthly (PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) indicates robust labor market conditions, increasing disposable income and driving positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% occurs but 5-day returns are negative in > 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.1% in 3 months), equity valuations contract due to higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% AND FEDFUNDS rise > 0.1% in 3 months
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.1% occurs but 20-day returns are positive in > 55% of cases.
